answers.assumptions: That the Oct 8 low would hold as support and that oversold meant a bounce was near. Support broke instead; oversold assets can keep falling in a downtrend.
answers.change_strategy: Be stricter on buying below both the 20-day and 50-day averages: require a sign the drop has stopped (for example a higher daily close) before entering. Keep the stop rule.
answers.evidence: Kraken daily OHLC levels, RSI from real daily closes, Standard Chartered RLUSD custody news (The Block), and the bearish Evernorth and ledger-bug stories, all recorded before the buy.
answers.hypothesis: XRP was oversold (RSI about 28) just above its Oct 8 low of 1.876; a bounce toward the 2.125 breakdown level was plausible, with a stop 1% under that low at 1.857685.
answers.process_luck_mistake: Mostly sound process: the trade passed every gate, was sized at about 10% of the account, and the stop did its job. Part bad luck in timing. One process weakness: stops are only checked when a run is active, so the Oct 15 intraday break went unseen and today's fill came in below the stop.
answers.rules_followed: Yes: position cap, risk per trade and crypto cap respected; stop placed by the written evidence-based rule; exit taken by the stop without overriding it.
answers.test_next_time: Track how often oversold-near-support crypto setups actually bounce within 1-3 weeks before trusting them again, and check whether the daily trend (below both averages) should block buys even when reward:risk passes.
answers.what_happened: XRP never bounced. It closed between 1.89 and 1.94 for three days, dipped to 1.825 intraday on Oct 15 while no run was active, then fell to about 1.84 today as crypto slid (Ether and Solana also down). The stop filled at about 1.842, below the 1.8577 stop (a gap), for -6.64 CAD (-6.6%).

lessons: Oversold is not the same as about to bounce; in a downtrend support can break.
Stops only checked during runs can fill below the planned price (gap risk).

answers.rules_followed: Yes: position size about 100 CAD, stop set below real support, and exit on the written invalidation rule. The stop only fires when a run is active, which is a weakness.
answers.test_next_time: Check whether buying 'oversold near support' works better when the bigger trend (20-day average) is also turning up, not falling.
